# Description

This is the R code used to run each Random Forest model. It also includes the model validation (cross-validation, OOB values, and Observed vs Predicted plots), variable importance analyses, explainable machine learning (h-statistic and partial dependence plots), and the code to reproduce our predictions using different time spans.

## Libraries

```{r}
pacman::p_load(tidymodels, tidyverse, future, doRNG,GGally, tictoc, pdp,foreach,doParallel, ranger, hstats, corrr ) 
```

## Data

This data set contains all three data sets used in the study, including species richness and predictors.

```{r}
data<-readRDS("all_data_star.rds")
names(data)

```

Filter the "DataSet" column to analyze individual data sets or omit filtering to use all data sets combined

```{r}
table(data$DataSet)
```

Filtering data set, example:

```{r}
data <- data[data$DataSet == "Atlases", ]
```

# Ramdom forest

## Model settings

#### Set the predictors and response

```{r}

responses<-"richness"

#first trial predictors

predictors<-c("tas","tmax","tmin","pr","AREA", "lon", "lat","start_year","time_span", "median_ndvi","Broad_leaved_forest", "Complex_cultivation_patterns",  "Construction_sites", "Coniferous_forest","Continuous_urban_fabric","Discontinuous_urban_fabric", "Green_urban_areas", "Land_principally_occupied_by_agriculture__with_significant_areas_of_natural_vegetation", "Mixed_forest", "Moors_and_heathland", "Natural_grasslands", "Pastures", "Transitional_woodland_shrub", "Water_bodies","Water_courses", "Protected_area")

#NOTE: Post-correlation analysis → replace with uncorrelated predictors only. See "Important Note"
```

#### Set partition, engine, and metrics

```{r}
split_prop<-3/4 #75% of data in training & 25% for validation
ml_engine<-"ranger"
ml_mode<-"regression"
ml_metrics<-metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae)
```

## Tuning parameters

```{r}
tuning_params<- expand.grid(
  mtry=c(5, 7,10,13,17), #number predictors, replace with the max. number of pred.
  trees=c(500,1000,1500, 2000, 2500, 3000),
  min_n=c(2,5)# Minimum number of samples required to split an internal node
)

NROW(tuning_params)
```

## Data preparation

```{r}
ml_data<-select(data,any_of(c(responses, predictors)))
```

### Check data plots

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(ml_data$AREA, ml_data$richness)
plot(ml_data$lat, ml_data$richness)
plot(ml_data$time_span, ml_data$richness)
plot(ml_data$AREA, ml_data$time_span)

```

## Preparing training and testing data

```{r}
set.seed(9872345)
ml_split<-initial_split(ml_data, prop = split_prop)

ml_split
```

## Create a cross-validation set for later use

```{r}
ml_cv<- vfold_cv(training(ml_split))
```

## Create recipe

```{r}

formula <- as.formula(paste(responses, paste(predictors, collapse = "+"), sep = "~"))

ml_recipe <- recipe(formula, data = ml_data) %>%
  # Remove NAs
  step_naomit()
```

# Create the model

```{r}
rf_model <- 
  # specify that the model is a random forest
  rand_forest() %>%
  # Parameters to be tuned
  set_args(mtry = tune(),
           trees = tune(),
           min_n = tune()) %>%
  # Select the modeling engine
  set_engine(engine = ml_engine, importance = "permutation") %>%
  # Select between regression and binary classification
  set_mode(ml_mode)
```

## Create a workflow

```{r}

rf_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  # add the recipe
  add_recipe(ml_recipe) %>%
  # add the model
  add_model(rf_model)

```

## Tune parameters

```{r}

num_cores <- 30  
plan(multisession, workers = num_cores)

tic()
# extract results
rf_tune_results <- rf_workflow %>%
  tune_grid(resamples = ml_cv, #Cross-validation data object
            # Grid of hyperparameters
            grid = tuning_params, 
            # Metrics to evaluate
            metrics = ml_metrics
            )
toc()

save.image("model.RData")
```

## Plot tunned parameters

```{r}
autoplot(rf_tune_results) 

```

## Collect and evaluate results

```{r}
rf_tune_results %>%
  collect_metrics()
```

## The very best of tunning

```{r}
param_final <- rf_tune_results %>%
  select_best(metric = "rmse")
print(param_final)

```

## Finalize workflow

```{r}
rf_workflow <- rf_workflow %>%
  finalize_workflow(param_final)
```

# Fit the final model to the training and testing data

```{r}
rf_fit <- rf_workflow %>%
  # fit on the training set and evaluate on test set
  last_fit(ml_split)
```

### R square et al.

```{r}
test_performance <- rf_fit %>% collect_metrics()
test_performance

```

# Variable Importance Plot (VIP)

```{r}
library(vip)
f_model <- extract_fit_parsnip(rf_fit)

# Plot variable importance
importance_scores<-vip(f_model$fit,  num_features = 27,geom = "col")
importance_scores

importance_scores$data <- importance_scores$data %>%
  mutate(Variable = ifelse(Variable == "Land_principally_occupied_by_agriculture__with_significant_areas_of_natural_vegetation", 
                           "Agr_NatVeg", Variable))


# Define a custom color scale with blue shades
blue_shades <- colorRampPalette(c("lightblue", "darkblue"))(15)

# Plot with custom blue shades
vip<-ggplot(importance_scores$data, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance, fill = Importance)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightblue", high = "darkblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "VIP_model ALL data", x = "Variables", y = "Importance")


#ggsave(plot=vip, "vip_all.png", bg="white")

vip

```

## Check correlations

Here is a way to rank the predictors according to their importance values and obtain the correlation matrix accordingly

```{r}
importance_all<-importance_scores[["data"]]%>%
  as.data.frame()
saveRDS(importance_all,"importance_all.rds")
```

```{r}
ml_train2<-ml_recipe%>% prep()%>% juice()


top_predictors <- importance_scores$data$Variable
print(top_predictors)


final_data <- ml_train2 %>%
  select(all_of(top_predictors))

library(corrr)

correlation_matrix <- final_data %>%
  correlate()
rplot(correlation_matrix) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

```{r}
# Convert the correlation matrix to a data frame
correlation_df <- correlation_matrix %>%
  stretch()


# Print the data frame
#print(correlation_df_first)
correlation_df<-as.data.frame(correlation_df)
correlation_df

#write.csv(correlation_df,"correlation_df_all.csv")
```

# Important Note

Following VIP analysis, we identified highly correlated predictors (\|r\| \> 0.7) and refitted the Random Forest model using only uncorrelated top predictors. Thus, to obtain the final model for each data set, you should modify the list of predictors accordingly and re-run the model. Before doing that, we suggest to delete all objects from the Global environment, and restart the R session, otherwise Rstudio could collapse.

## Model performance

### OOB

```{r}

ranger_model <- extract_fit_parsnip(rf_fit)$fit

oob_r2 <- ranger_model$r.squared
print(oob_r2)

oob_mse <- ranger_model$prediction.error
print(oob_mse)
```

### CV

```{r}
ml_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae)

set.seed(9872345)
cv_results <- rf_workflow %>%
  fit_resamples(
    resamples = ml_cv,
    metrics = ml_metrics,
    control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
  )

cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(cv_results)
print(cv_metrics)
```

### Observed vs. predicted

```{r}

resultados <- collect_predictions(rf_fit)

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(resultados, aes(x = .pred, y = richness)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Predicted", y = "Observed", title = "Observed vs Predicted") +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Interactions

### HSTATS

```{r}

ml_train2<-ml_recipe%>% prep()%>% juice()


set.seed(782)
system.time(
  s <- hstats(f_model, X = ml_train2)  
)

s

plot(s) 
```

### Partial Dependence Plots

Here some examples:

```{r}
pd <- partial_dep(f_model, v = c("AREA", "time_span"), X = ml_train2, grid_size = 500)
plot(pd)
plot(pd, d2_geom = "line", show_points = FALSE)

```

```{r}
wb <- partial_dep(f_model, v = c("Water_bodies", "time_span"), X = ml_train2, grid_size = 500)
plot(wb)
plot(wb, d2_geom = "line", show_points = FALSE)

```

# PREDICTIONS

Please note that the predictions showed in the study were made based on the **JPSP_points model**. Here, we include the data set used to make the predictions shown in the study and the code use it after running the **JPSP_points model**.

## Libraries

```{r}
pacman::p_load(tidymodels, dplyr, sf,RCzechia,ggplot2)
```

## Data

This data set includes all the predictor variables used in the model JPSP_points but calculated

```{r}
prediction_data<-readRDS("prediction_data.rds")

```

Predictors

```{r}
predictors<-c("pr","AREA", "lon", "lat","start_year","time_span", "median_ndvi","Broad_leaved_forest", "Complex_cultivation_patterns",  "Construction_sites", "Coniferous_forest","Green_urban_areas", "Land_principally_occupied_by_agriculture__with_significant_areas_of_natural_vegetation", "Mixed_forest", "Moors_and_heathland", "Natural_grasslands", "Pastures", "Transitional_woodland_shrub", "Water_bodies","Water_courses", "Protected_area")

```

## Predict

```{r}

modelo_rf<-extract_workflow(rf_fit)# this should be rf_fit of the JPSP_points model

predicciones <- predict(modelo_rf, new_data = prediction_data)

predictions <- predict(modelo_rf, new_data = prediction_data) %>%
  bind_cols(prediction_data)

```

```{r}

resultados <- data.frame(
  time_span = prediction_data$time_span,
  lat = prediction_data$lat,
  lon = prediction_data$lon,
  id = prediction_data$id,
  richness_predicha = predicciones
)

resultados_filtrados <- resultados %>%
  filter(time_span %in% c(1, 5, 15))

```

Min and max

```{r}
min_pred <- min(resultados$.pred, na.rm = TRUE)
max_pred <- max(resultados$.pred, na.rm = TRUE)

```

CZ shape file

```{r}
cz_shp <- st_read("CZE_adm0.shp")
```

### Map time span 1yr

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(dplyr)

map_1yr <- ggplot(filter(resultados, time_span == 1), aes(x = lon, y = lat, color = .pred)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1, name = "species richness",limits = c(min_pred, max_pred)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = unit(c(1, 1, 1, 1), "cm")
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = cz_shp, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE)+
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = max(resultados$lon),     
    y = max(resultados$lat),     
    label = "1 year",
    hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
    size = 7, fontface = "bold"
  )
map_1yr
```

## Hotspots

```{r}
resultados <- resultados %>%
  group_by(time_span) %>%
  mutate(hotspots = as.integer(.pred >= quantile(.pred, probs = 0.9))) %>%
  ungroup()

```

### 1 year

```{r}
hotspots_1yr2 <- ggplot(filter(resultados, time_span == 1), aes(x = lon, y = lat)) +
  #geom_point(aes(color = .pred), size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +  # Base
  geom_point(data = . %>% filter(hotspots == 1),  # Hotspots
             color = "#F1605DFF", size = 2, shape = 19, stroke = 1) +
   scale_color_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1, name = "species richness",limits = c(min_pred, max_pred)) +
  labs( x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = unit(c(1, 1, 1, 1), "cm") # Márgenes iguales para uniformidad
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = cz_shp, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE)+
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = max(resultados$lon),     # Usa el mínimo valor de lon para la izquierda
    y = max(resultados$lat),     # Usa el máximo valor de lat para arriba
    label = "1 year",
    hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
    size = 7, fontface = "bold"
  )

hotspots_1yr2

```

## Coldspots

```{r}
resultados <- resultados %>%
  group_by(time_span) %>%
  # Ordenamos ascendentemente por .pred
  mutate(coldspots = as.integer(row_number(.pred) <= floor(n() * 0.1))) %>%
  ungroup()

```
